source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This Flexential facility is in one of the company national markets confirmed on its own homepage covering Oregon (Portland/Hillsboro), Texas (Dallas, Plano, Richardson), Ohio (West Chester, Cincinnati market), Kentucky (Louisville), Pennsylvania (Allentown, Collegeville, Philadelphia market), Virginia (Richmond), Minnesota (Chaska, Minneapolis market), and Arizona (Phoenix). Flexential was formed from the 2017 merger of ViaWest, founded 1999, and Peak 10, founded 2000, followed by a 2018 rebrand to Flexential. The company reports 40 plus data centers across 18 national markets, 3 million plus square feet of facilities, an 800 million dollar expansion investment, and a planned new campus on 110 acres in Kaufman County near Dallas. This specific state cluster was confirmed as an active Flexential market on the company own site, but no market specific founding, acquisition, or building history distinct from the general ViaWest and Peak 10 company story was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Flexential Minneapolis - Chaska publishes 9 MW of IT capacity, the only operator-disclosed megawatt figure among 13 mapped Minnesota facilities, making its actual scale in the state unknown from public operator data.

The 9 MW capacity spans 160,838 square feet of technical space. Whether this facility hosts AI training or general colocation matters for power density: at 40 kW per rack, typical for AI training, 9 MW supports roughly 225 racks; at 10 kW per rack, typical for colocation, the same power supports roughly 900 racks. The operator publishes no allocation breakdown, so which workload mix occupies the space cannot be determined from available facts.

Seven certifications qualify the facility for regulated workloads: financial and operational controls auditing under SOC 1 and SOC 2; payment card data under PCI DSS; export-controlled defense and aerospace work under ITAR; federal security alignment under NIST 800-53; and healthcare information under HITRUST. These credentials indicate qualified tenancy rather than capacity or actual allocation. No tenant names are published.

Twelve other mapped Minnesota facilities publish no capacity figures, making state-level rankings of disclosed capacity unreliable proxies for actual facility scale. This facility's ranking as the largest Minnesota facility by published spec reflects publication practice among operators rather than physical supremacy in the region.
